text:
Alex Kim: putting a draft PRD snippet here for Dedicated Capacity SLA + autoscaling. Want quick feedback on targets + acceptance criteria.
Priya Patel: looking now — can you TL;DR the hard constraints?
Alex Kim: TL;DR: 99.9% p99 latency <= 300ms for text-gen baseline (seq len 256), throughput sizing per reserved GPU pool with headroom 1.5x expected peak, autoscale burst to handle 3x short spikes.
Jamie Ortega: 300ms p99 is aggressive for some models. Which model families are we guaranteeing? small/med/large?
Alex Kim: initial scope: verified Redwood-optimized Llama 65B-qat (quantized) and a 7B standard variant. Doc will call out model-specific SLAs; baseline refers to 7B-equivalent.
Morgan Lee: and what about cold-starts / cache warm-up? need SLO exceptions for first 60s after deploy or pool scale-up.
Alex Kim: good call — acceptance criteria will include "grace window": first 60s after scale/rollout exempt from strict p99. Add rollback policy if >1% of requests hit errors in that window.
Sam Gupta: sales ask: customers want guaranteed throughput per-commitment (e.g., reserved vGPU-hours) — how do we map SLA to contracts?
Alex Kim: propose mapping: commit tier A: 1000 tokens/s sustained per pool, tier B: 5000 tokens/s, with autoscale headroom = 1.5x. Legal can convert to RUs in contract.
Priya Patel: for autoscale rules we should avoid CPU-based triggers. Prefer request-rate + queue-depth + GPU-util heuristics. Example:
```
policy: 
  min_instances: 1
  max_instances: 10
  scale_up_if: avg_qps > 800 OR queue_depth > 50 OR gpu_util > 75%
  scale_down_if: avg_qps < 300 AND gpu_util < 40% for 120s
  burst_mode: allow immediate add up to +3 instances if sustained spike > 3s
```
Jamie Ortega: looks good. Add cooldown timers and a rate limiter for scale ops so we don't thrash. also consider pre-warming for scheduled high traffic.
Morgan Lee: Ops acceptance criteria:
- can maintain p99 latency target in 95% of synthetic workload runs that model customer traffic patterns
- autoscale triggers add nodes within 8s median on sustained spike
- no error-rate regressions vs baseline >0.5%
- observability: per-route latency + per-token cost dashboards available
Alex Kim: I'm adding those to the PRD. Edge cases to call out: model variant fallback, partial capacity loss (N+1 failure), region failover, noisy neighbor on shared infra.
Priya Patel: for model fallback, require semantic compatibility (same tokenizer + output format). Fallback path must be tested end-to-end in canary.
Sam Gupta: customer asks also for a SLA credit formula when we miss targets. Do we want to list that now or defer to sales/legal?
Alex Kim: defer but include requirement: "document credit calculation and escalation path" in the PRD.
Jamie Ortega: ops detail: capacity sizing guidance for customers provisioning dedicated pools:
- baseline per-gpu throughput: 7B ~ 300 rps, 13B ~ 140 rps, 65B ~ 30 rps (seq=256, temp=0.2)
- recommend commit sizing = expected_peak_rps * 1.5 / per-gpu throughput
Morgan Lee: add stability test checklist: cold-start run, sustained 4h soak at 90% target, failure injection (remove 1 GPU) and observe failover.
Alex Kim: acceptance checklist draft (short):
1) benchmark results attached for supported models
2) autoscale policy validated in staging (no thrash)
3) monitoring dashboards + alert runbooks created
4) rollback & fallback tested in canary
5) SLA wording drafted for contracts
Jamie Ortega: tiny nit: change p99 to p99.5 for highest tier? customers asking. Might be separate tier.
Alex Kim: noted — will add tiered SLA options (p99.5 premium).
Priya Patel: can we add a small config snippet for fallback routing?
```
fallback: 
  - priority: same-model-smaller-shard
  - priority: distill-7b-compatible
  - on_capacity_loss: return 503 + X-Redwood-Fallback-Used header
```
Morgan Lee: add the header + metric so we can alert on fallback rate >0.1%.
Alex Kim: thanks all. I'll update PRD with these bits and post a new link. If no blockers, aim to ship PRD to eng review by EOD Friday. :shipit:
deploy-bot: new staging autoscale test run queued (#2026).
Priya Patel: thumbs up. I can take the staging run and run the soak tests on Monday. :eyes:
